summary: British colonial officer Robert Baden-Powell founded Scouting in 1907 while refusing to screen scoutmasters and quietly dismissing abusers, a pattern the Boy Scouts of America kept for a century until abuse claims drove it into bankruptcy in 2020.

evidence.note: fights in the Second Matabele War in 1896; execution of a surrendered chief
commands the garrison through the long siege of Mafeking in the Boer War
allegations he starved and expelled Black residents during the siege, and the historians' debate
rewrites his scouting manual in 1907 and runs the first trial boy camp
rejects proposals to screen scoutmasters so the movement can grow faster
abusive camp doctor at Gilwell is let go quietly instead of reported to police
death in 1941; patterns he set carry on in the organization
BSA starts its ineligible volunteer files in 1919, including the abuse subset
long Southern California case of an expelled leader who rejoins troops for years
BSA refuses background checks in the 1980s and lobbies against state requirements
over 100,000 alleged victims by late 2020, bankruptcy and campground sales

notes: Baden-Powell and the BSA treated as co-primary: part 1 is his biography, part 2 is the BSA abuse history. Roles: no id for founding a youth movement; activist-organizer is the closest. No theme for institutional cover-up or lobbying against statute-of-limitation reform. Seton gets only a few minutes, so he is a keyword. Covered span ends at the 2020 claims count and bankruptcy.
